title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a section of Grothendieck's notes on Gauss–Manin connections. S/T is a smooth morphism (or at least one with good principal parts). E is a quasi-coherent O_S-module (a vector bundle) with an integrable connection, or later with a stratification relative to T.

End of §1 (continuing from the previous page). H^1_DR(S,E) has been interpreted as classifying E-torsors P equipped with a connection d_P compatible with that of E.
- The connections on a given torsor P correspond to the homomorphisms (17) that satisfy the first relation (18).
- The second relation in (18) cuts these down to the integrable connections.
- The automorphisms of P compatible with d_P form a group, namely the group of translations by horizontal sections of E, i.e. H^0_DR(S,E) = Γ(S,E)^∇.
- These descriptions are functorial in E and compatible with inverse images (base change).
This is the standard torsor (Čech/Giraud-style) reading of H^0 and H^1 in the 'de Rham' coefficient category. Equivalently, H^1_DR(S,E) = Ext^1(O_S,E) in the category of modules with integrable connection, with extensions replaced by affine torsors.

§2 'Stratifications sur torseurs affines'. Now suppose E carries a stratification relative to T, in Grothendieck's sense: an infinite-order descent datum on the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal, i.e. a crystal on the stratifying site.
- E then defines a sheaf of stratified sections E_strat on the stratifying site (S/T)_strat.
- (19) defines H^*_strat(S,E) := H^*((S/T)_strat, E_strat).
- (20) An infinitesimal gluing datum ('donnée de recollement') of order ∞ on E is the same as an O_S-linear map δ^∞_E : E → P^∞_{S/T}(E), where P^∞ is the module of principal parts of infinite order (EGA IV 16).
- (21) The normalisation is ε_E∘δ^∞_E = id_E, where ε is the augmentation P^∞(E) → E.
- (22) He then sets d^+_E = d^∞_E − δ^∞_E : E → P^∞_{S/T}(E)^+, with values in the augmentation ideal. Here d^∞_E is the canonical (Taylor, non-linear) map x ↦ 1⊗x, and δ^∞_E is the twisted one.

On the next page, the reduction of d^+_E to P^1(E)^+ ≅ E⊗Ω^1 gives the associated connection, which is integrable when the gluing datum is a stratification. This yields H^*_strat → H^*_DR. The stratification is then encoded as a cosimplicial comodule C^n(E) built from the formal completion of the diagonal in (S/T)^{n+1}; this is the Čech–Alexander complex.

The purpose of all this is to repeat the torsor interpretation of H^0 and H^1 for stratified (crystalline-type) cohomology, and to compare it with de Rham cohomology. That comparison feeds the construction of the Gauss–Manin connection via the stratifying/crystalline site.
errors: Equation numbering is inconsistent: the definition of d^+_E should be (22), since the next page refers to '(22)'; the transcription repeats (21).

Sign/naming convention: d^∞_E denotes the canonical Taylor map and δ^∞_E the gluing map. The margin note's identification of δ_E with 'the connection' is loose, since the connection proper is d^+_E reduced mod the square of the augmentation ideal.

ideas.what: H^0_DR(S,E) as the automorphism group of an affine E-torsor with compatible connection; H^1_DR as classifying such torsors with integrable connection
ideas.modern_name: torsor interpretation of H^1 / Ext^1 in the category of D-modules (integrable connections)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Grothendieck school; Giraud for nonabelian H^1)
ideas.where_published: possibly implicit in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Cohomology of the stratifying site H^*_strat(S,E) = H^*((S/T)_strat, E_strat)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés 1968); Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (LNM 407)

ideas.what: Infinite-order gluing datum as δ^∞_E : E → P^∞_{S/T}(E) with ε∘δ = id; d^+ = d^∞ − δ^∞ into the augmentation ideal, reducing to the connection
ideas.modern_name: hyper-stratification / Taylor map description of stratifications

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Grothendieck-school material on stratifications, principal parts and torsor interpretations of de Rham/stratified cohomology, all well documented (Dix exposés, Berthelot). Nothing new appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: The struck/replaced line reads roughly 'Une donnée de recollement infinitésimale d'ordre ∞ sur E revient à la donnée d'un homomorphisme', not 'Une donnée de stratification ... E variant de la donnée'. The next page confirms the term 'donnée de recollement'.
The equation defining d^+_E is presumably numbered (22), not (21), per the next page's reference to '(22)'.

'Les [faisceaux des] automorphismes de P compatibles avec d_P ... forment le groupe ... des sections horizontales de E, i.e. H^0_DR(S,E)': the inserted word above 'automorphismes' looks like 'faisceaux des'.
In the margin, 'P^∞_{S/T}(E)^+, idéal d'augmentation' is correct; the note 'On dit parfois que δ_E est la connexion' is partially illegible ('δ_E' is uncertain).
